EXPLANATION: The spectrum is characteristic of a mono-substituted benzene:

• Very strong ring-breathing band at 1001 cm⁻¹ and double ring C=C stretches at 1601/1576 cm⁻¹ are the classic Raman fingerprint of a mono-substituted phenyl ring.  
• The strong CH-out-of-plane bend of a mono-substituted ring normally appears near 690 cm⁻¹ – matching the 683 cm⁻¹ peak.  
• The ether C–O–C stretches of an alkyl-aryl ether occur near 1200 cm⁻¹ (aryl-O) and 1050–1100 cm⁻¹ (alkyl-O); these correspond well to the 1206 cm⁻¹ and 1083 cm⁻¹ peaks.  
• Aliphatic and aromatic C–H stretches are present at 2921 cm⁻¹ and 3073 cm⁻¹.  
• Two C–Cl stretching modes in a chloroethyl group are expected around 550–700 cm⁻¹ and 500 cm⁻¹, rationalising the 683 cm⁻¹ and 514 cm⁻¹ peaks.

Among the candidates, only candidate 5 (ClCCOc1ccccc1) is a mono-substituted phenyl ether bearing a chloroethyl chain, fitting all key vibrational features without requiring additional functional-group bands (no OH/NH stretch observed).
